test_title: PYST 36: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In the Indian parliamentary system, who has the authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha before its term expires?

options.text: The Prime Minister advises the President to dissolve it.
The Council of Ministers passes a resolution.
The Chief Justice of India orders dissolution.
The Speaker of Lok Sabha takes the decision.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Prime Minister advises the President to dissolve it.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Indian parliamentary system, the **President of India** holds the formal authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• The dissolution of the Lok Sabha typically occurs **on the advice of the Prime Minister** and the Council of Ministers.
 
• This advice is binding on the President as per the principles of a parliamentary democracy where the President acts on the advice of the Cabinet.
 
• Dissolution can occur **before the completion of the Lok Sabha's five-year term** or upon its natural expiry.
 
• This process is crucial for initiating **fresh general elections** and ensuring democratic continuity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's Parliament and is composed of representatives directly elected by the people of India.
 
• It has a term of **five years**, unless dissolved sooner.
 
• It is responsible for enacting laws, controlling finances, and scrutinizing the work of the executive.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution of Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• Dissolution refers to the complete termination of the Lok Sabha's current term, leading to general elections.
 
• It can be classified into **automatic dissolution** (when the term ends) or **premature dissolution** (upon the Prime Minister's advice).
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President of India, as the constitutional head, formally dissolves the Lok Sabha.
 
• The President acts based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Dissolution:**
 
 
• Dissolution ensures the periodic renewal of the democratic mandate through elections.
 
• It provides an opportunity for the electorate to evaluate the performance of the government.
